mechanism_narrative: When the monthly FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25 percentage points over the next month, the S&P 500 20-day forward return tends to be negative due to expectations of tighter policy and reduced risk appetite.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25pp in the following month
regime_hint: early stage of a tightening cycle
failure_condition: Over a 5-year window, no significant negative 20-day forward return occurs after such FEDFUNDS increases when other risk factors are neutral.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in CPIAUCSL (inflation) by at least 0.5% over two consecutive months predicts a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as investors anticipate lower future rate hikes.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases by ≥0.5% over two consecutive months
failure_condition: In regimes with strong growth signals, the 60-day forward return does not outperform a 5% risk-free rate benchmark after inflation declines.

mechanism_narrative: When PAYEMS rises by more than 2,000 monthly jobs over three months, the S&P 20-day forward return is expected to be positive as labor market strength supports equity risk appetite.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >2,000 in three consecutive months
failure_condition: During periods of high inflation or elevated rates, the 20-day forward return does not exceed the market risk premium estimate.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO by at least 1% while HOUST rises by at least 5% signals a structural shift toward demand-driven production, which tends to boost S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO ↓ ≥1% AND HOUST ↑ ≥5% in the same month
regime_hint: transition from supply shock to demand recovery
failure_condition: The interaction is not statistically significant in backtests using Granger causality for 2005-2024 period.

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS falls by more than 10% in a month, the S&P 500 60-day forward return is predicted to be negative due to elevated concerns about corporate credit and consumer spending.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases by >10% in a single month
failure_condition: No significant negative 60-day forward return occurs after such RSAFS declines in non-stress macro regimes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in UNRATE below 4% for two consecutive months predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as higher labor costs suppress corporate earnings expectations.
failure_condition: In periods of strong GDP growth, the forward return does not remain negative after UNRATE normalization.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains above 4% for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 60-day forward return tends to be negative due to persistent policy tightening and reduced liquidity.
failure_condition: No significant negative 60-day forward return occurs when other risk factors (e.g., equities, bonds) are also falling.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly convergence of INDPRO and GDPC1 (industrial production lag vs. billings) above their 12-month moving averages signals a supply-demand balance improving, which is associated with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > INDPRO_12MA AND GDPC1 > GDPC1_12MA in the same month
failure_condition: The interaction is not predictive in periods where macroeconomic news is dominated by external shocks unrelated to domestic supply.
